questions.question: A1 alone can do a work in 12 days and A2 alone can do the same work in 15 days. With help of A3, they finish the same work in 5 days. In how many days A3 alone can do the same work ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A1 does the work in 12 days.

A2 does the same work in 15 days.

A1, A2, and A3 together do the work in 5 days.

**Formula:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 5) = 60 units

Efficiency of A1 = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of A2 = 60/15 = 4

Efficiency of A1 + A2 + A3 = 60/5 = 12

Efficiency of A3 = (Efficiency of A1 + A2 + A3) - (Efficiency of A1 + A2)

⇒ Efficiency of A3 = 12 - 9 = 3

Time taken by A3 to complete the work = 60/3 = 20 days

**Therefore, A3 alone can do the work in 20 days.**

questions.question: Mahesh. Suresh and Raju together can complete a work in 18 days. Mahesh and Suresh together can complete the same work in 72 days. Raju alone can finish the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju together do the work in 18 days.

Mahesh and Suresh together do the same work in 72 days.

Formula:

Work = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

Total work = LCM(18, 72) = 72 units

Efficiency of Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju = 72/18 = 4

Efficiency of Mahesh and Suresh = 72/72 = 1

Efficiency of Raju = (Efficiency of Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju) - (Efficiency of Mahesh and Suresh)

⇒ Efficiency of A3 = 4 - 1 = 3

Time taken by Raju to complete the work = 72/3 = 24 days

Therefore, Raju alone can do the work in 24 days.

questions.question: What will be the length of longest diagonal of the cuboid having length 13 cm width 11 cm and height 20 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of cuboid = 13 cm

Width of cuboid = 11 cm

Height of cuboid = 20 cm

**Formula: **

The longest diagonal of a cuboid = √(length² + width² + height²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Diagonal = √(13² + 11² + 20²)

⇒ Diagonal = √(169 + 121 + 400)

Diagonal = √(690) = 26.2 cm

**Therefore, the length of the longest diagonal of the cuboid is approximately 26.27 cm.**

questions.question: What is the average of the first four multiples of 6?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First four multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24.

**Formula: **

Average = (Sum of terms)/(Number of terms)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Average = (6 + 12 + 18 + 24)/4

⇒ Average = 60/4

Average = 15

**Therefore, the average of the first four multiples of 6 is 15.**

questions.question: What will be the HCF of the following set of numbers: 30, 45, 150, ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The set of numbers is 30, 45, 150.

**Formula:**

Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the largest number that divides each of the given numbers.

**Calculation:**

The factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30.

The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45.

The factors of 150 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 25, 30, 50, 75, 150.

The common factors of 30, 45, and 150 are 1, 3, 5, 15.

HCF = 15

**Therefore, the HCF of the numbers 30, 45, and 150 is 15.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2000 will become Rs. 2400 in 12 months at some rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 2000

Amount (A) = Rs. 2400

Time (T) = 1 year

**Formula: **

Simple Interest = (Amount - Principal)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Interest = 2400 - 2000 = Rs. 400

Then, Rate (R) = (Interest/(Principal × Time)) × 100

⇒ Rate = (400/(2000 × 1)) × 100

Rate = 20%

**Therefore, the rate of interest per annum is 20%.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns 20% profit on his goods. He lost 20% of his goods during a theft. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit percentage = 20%
Percentage of goods lost = 20%

**Formula:**

The formula for calculating loss percentage is (Loss / Cost Price) × 100.

**Calculation:**

Initial Cost Price (CP) = 1 unit (for simplicity)

Initial Selling Price (SP) = CP + (Profit % of CP) ⇒ 1 + 0.2 × 1 = 1.2 units

Percentage of goods remaining = 100% - 20% = 80%

CP of remaining goods = 0.8 × 1 = 0.8 units

SP of remaining goods = 0.8 × 1.2 = 0.96 units

Loss = CP - SP ⇒ 1 - 0.96 = 0.04 units

Loss percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100 ⇒ (0.04 / 1) × 100 = 4%

**Therefore, the shopkeeper has a loss of 4%.**

questions.question: What is the value of (1)/(2) of (16)/(5)+(1)/(8) of (24)/(9) times (18)/(12)-(5)/(8) ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The expression is 1/2 of 16/5 + 1/8 of 24/9 × 18/12 - 5/8

Concept used:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47485e25d1b30c57dc271863db8b99be0c8e209069b2596cc885911d898a8a78.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Evaluate the operations within parentheses first, according to the BODMAS rule.

⇒ 1/2 × 16/5 + 1/8 × 24/9 × 18/12 - 5/8

⇒ 8/5 + 1/3 × 18/12 - 5/8

⇒ 8/5 + 1/2 - 5/8

⇒ (64 + 20 - 25)/40

⇒ 59/40

**∴ The value of given expression is 59/40.**

questions.question: What will be the LCM of 37, 41?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The numbers are 37, 41.

**Formula:**

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two prime numbers is their product.

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM = 37 × 41

LCM = 1517

**Therefore, the LCM of 37 and 41 is 1517.**

questions.question: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is 17 ∶ 15. If path is 40 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of circumferences of two circles is identical to the ratio of their radii.

Ratio of outer radius (R) to inner radius (r) = 17 ∶ 15

Width of the path in ratio units = 17 − 15 = 2 units.

Given width = 40 metres, so 2 units = 40 metres ⇒ 1 unit = 20 metres.

Inner radius = 15 units = 15 × 20 = 300 metres.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of outer and inner circumference = 17 ∶ 15

Width of the path = 40 metres

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2×π×r

Width of circular path = R − r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/901a6739e9dc59f8882b395fec41f837af89839e1d5def8de74be8db74beb14f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the outer radius be R and the inner radius be r.

⇒ Ratio of circumferences = (2×π×R) ÷ (2×π×r)

⇒ R / r = 17 / 15

⇒ Let R = 17x and r = 15x

⇒ Width of the circular path = Outer Radius − Inner Radius

⇒ 17x − 15x = 40

⇒ 2x = 40

⇒ x = 20

⇒ Inner radius (r) = 15x = 15 × 20 = 300 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Path

The total area located strictly between two concentric circles is given by Area = π×(R² − r²), where R and r are the respective outer and inner radii.

Length of an Arc

An arc is a fraction of the full circumference. The length is determined by the central angle θ: (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The region bounded by two radii and an adjoining arc is called a sector. Its area is: (θ ÷ 360) × πr².

questions.question: If A ∶ B = 3 ∶ 2, B ∶ C = 7 ∶ 5 and C ∶ D = 10 ∶ 3, then what is A ∶ D equal to?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A ∶ B = 3 ∶ 2

B ∶ C = 7 ∶ 5

C ∶ D = 10 ∶ 3

**Formula:**

To find the ratio A : D, we multiply the three given ratios.

**Calculation:**

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C ∶ D = 21 : 14 : 10 : 3

⇒ A ∶ D = 21 : 3 = 7 : 1

**Therefor the ratio of A : D = 7 : 1.**

questions.question: Find compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 8000

Rate of interest (R) = 15% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula:**

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)² - P

**Calculation:**

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1 + 15/100)² - 8000

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1.15)² - 8000

Compound Interest = Rs. 2580

**Therefore, the compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is Rs. 2580.**

questions.question: Manny bought an AC for Rs. 12000 and paid Rs. 400 for transportation. Then he sold it for Rs. 14000. Find his profit %.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (C.P.) = Rs. 12000 + Rs. 400 = Rs. 12400

Selling Price (S.P.) = Rs. 14000

**Formula:**

Profit % = [(S.P. - C.P.)/C.P.] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit % = [(14000 - 12400)/12400] × 100

Profit % = 12.9%

**Therefore, the profit percentage is 12.9%.**

questions.question: Rs. 1800 is divided among A and B in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 respectively. What is the share of A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The total amount = Rs. 1800

The ratio of shares of A and B = 2 ∶ 3

**Formula:**

The share of each person is proportional to their ratio.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total parts in the ratio = 2 + 3 = 5

⇒ Each part = Total amount / Total parts in the ratio = 1800 / 5

⇒ The share of A = 2 × Each part

The share of A = Rs. 720

**Therefore, the share of A is Rs. 720.**

questions.question: Anita scored 36 marks out of 120 but later her teacher increased 6 marks for her. What will be the increase in her percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original marks = 36

Increased marks = 6

Total marks = 120

**Formula:**

Percentage increase = (Increase/Total marks) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Percentage increase = (6/120) × 100

Percentage increase = 5%

**Therefore, the increase in her percentage is 5%.**

questions.question: Working 12 hours per day. Raj can complete a work in 12 days. How many hours per day he should work so as to finish the same work in 9 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Raj works 12 hours/day for 12 days to complete the work

**Formula:**

Total work = Days × Hours/day

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work = 12 days × 12 hours/day

⇒ If he has to finish the same work in 9 days, hours/day = Total work / 9 days

Hours/day = 16 hours/day

**Therefore, he should work 16 hours per day to finish the work in 9 days.**

questions.question: A car has to cover a distance of 288 km in 20 hours. If it covers half of the journey in 1/5th of the time, find the speed to cover the remaining distance in the time left.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 288 km

Total time = 20 hours

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Half the distance = 288 km / 2 = 144 km

⇒ Time taken for half the distance = 1/5th of total time = 20 hours / 5 = 4 hours

⇒ Remaining distance = 144 km

⇒ Remaining time = 20 hours - 4 hours = 16 hours

⇒ Speed for remaining distance = Remaining distance / Remaining time

Speed = 9 km/hr

**Therefore, the speed to cover the remaining distance in the time left is 9 km/hr.**

questions.question: The radius of a right circular cylinder is thrice of its height. If the height of the cylinder is 3.5 cm, then what is the volume of cylinder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height (h) of the cylinder = 3.5 cm

Radius (r) of the cylinder = 3 × h = 3 × 3.5 cm = 10.5 cm

**Formula:**

Volume of the cylinder (V) = πr²h

**Calculation:**

⇒ V = π × (10.5 cm)² × 3.5 cm

V = 1212.75 cm³

**Therefore, the volume of the cylinder is 1212.75 cm³.**

questions.question: The cost price of the box of pens is Rs. 400. The shopkeeper gave 10% of discount on the cost price. What will be the selling price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (C.P.) of a box of pens = Rs. 400

Discount given = 10% of C.P.

**Formula: **

Selling Price (S.P.) = C.P. - Discount

**Calculation:**

⇒ Discount = 10/100 × Rs. 400 = Rs. 40

⇒ S.P. = C.P. - Discount = Rs. 400 - Rs. 40

S.P. = Rs. 360

**Therefore, the selling price of the box of pens will be Rs. 360.**
